data.claim: A list knob in a lower config layer replaces the higher layer's list and DROPS entries the higher layer had set with no note (D-config-layer-order: lists replace).
data.falsifier: If stderr names no dropped entry and cfg records none when local is a strict subset of file, the silent-drop holds.
data.mechanism: Config._apply_knob setattr replaces any list the lower file/local/env layer had set; nothing compares the new list to the layer above.
data.probe: tmp root file layer [4 standing rules] + local [pins_regenerate]; Config.load(root); read stderr and cfg.dropped_members
data.probe_output: stderr names approvals.policy dropped entries (4 standing rules, set by the file layer); cfg.dropped_members carries the note.
data.question: Does a lower config layer's list silently drop the higher layer's list entries?

evidence.note: research R0d05177ff7 CONFIRMED: a lower config layer's list silently drops the higher layer's entries; probed Config.load on a tmp root (file layer 4 standing rules, local [pins_regenerate]) and reproduced the silent drop.

r-tighten-only (a layer may tighten, never silently loosen) and D-config-layer-order (later layers win; lists replace) govern ddflow/config/**; applied: detect dropped list entries in Config._apply_knob, name them at load (_warn.py) and in doctor (configcompat.py).

commits 6d7753e2f (warn when a lower config layer's list drops a higher layer's entries) + ae4c8a7e5 (move detection into Config._note_dropped to stay under the CC guard); regression test tests/test_config_layers.py (4 tests) fails on unfixed code (Config lacks dropped_members / _WARNED_DROPPED), passes on fixed.

chunk_findings.detail: `_dropped_list_entries` accepts arbitrary list entries and its docstring explicitly says the elements “need not be hashable,” but `_note_dropped` joins the returned raw entries with `', '.join(dropped)`, which requires every entry to be a `str`. Given a list knob whose dropped entries are not strings (for example the unhashable list entries the docstring allows: `below = [[1], [2]]`, `value = []`), `_dropped_list_entries` returns `[[1], [2]]` and `_note_dropped` raises `TypeError: sequence item 0: expected str instance, list found` during config load instead of recording the intended note.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_core.py:_note_dropped

chunk_findings.detail: The warn-once memo is keyed by the knob name before the first colon, not by the actual dropped entries. In a long-running ddflow process that reloads config (the docstring itself mentions MCP replies, so a server/daemon is plausible), the first load that drops `skip_after_unavailable`, `complete_unavailable`, and `claim_unavailable` adds `(root, "approvals.policy")` to `_WARNED_DROPPED`. If the operator then edits the local layer so it instead drops `complete_unavailable`/`claim_unavailable` but keeps `skip_after_unavailable`, the next `Config.load` will have those new dropped entries in `cfg.dropped_members`, but `_warn_dropped` will suppress the stderr note because the same key was already warned. The newly loosened entries are then silent at load, contrary to r-tighten-only: a lower layer may tighten, never silently loosen.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/config/_warn.py:_warn_dropped

data.probe: committed 78e4ca255: _note_dropped now joins str(e) for each dropped entry, so a dropped docs.extract dict entry is stringified not joined raw; test test_a_dropped_non_string_entry_is_stringified_not_raised passes.

data.probe: committed 78e4ca255: _WARNED_DROPPED keys on the whole note now, so a changed drop set warns again; test test_a_changed_dropped_set_is_said_again passes.
